programmes.d: Mikey goes on a Venezuelan treasure hunt for a rare CL-215 waterbomber, and new pilots Andrew and Graeme face their toughest test yet - flying with irascible boss Joe McBryan.

Buffalo launches an all-out campaign to airlift 100,000lbs of essential goods to cut-off northern communities, Justin helps a Mountie move and expectant parents Rod and Sasha show off their 3D ultrasound.
Crusty mechanic Chuck scrambles to ready the Electra for a mission to the High Arctic, and former rampie Audrey returns to Buffalo and reignites the battle of the sexes.
A multi-stop mission to the Far North pits Devan, Scott and Adam in an ongoing battle for fuel and oil as they circuit their destinations.

Young pilots AJ and Andrew get the chance of a lifetime to fly the DC-3 mounted on snow skis, and tension mounts across the company as Buffalo’s Mackenzie Valley food mail delivery contract is up for renewal.
Buffalo flies the Stanley Cup on a tour of the North, and a licence suspension has Joe looking for a captain to replace him on the passenger run he’s flown for almost 30 years.
Chief pilot Arnie lands the DC-3 on a homemade sand strip at a remote lodge. Electra expert Chuck faces off with a stubborn power unit, and Rod's wife Sasha goes into labour.
When thunderstorms and a shaky engine threaten a charter to Whitehorse, Joe pulls out all the stops to get the passengers to their destination.
A potential Electra plane purchase in Coventry, England has Joe showing Mikey the ropes of international business.
While training pilots for the upcoming fire season, chief pilot Arnie makes an unexpected announcement.
A shipment of medical equipment takes a turn for the weird when Jenn learns her load is a LOT different than expected.
Jarrett, single-handedly almost ruins the west coast art scene when he hauls an odd sculpture to its various photo shoot locations in the Bay area.
Jessica finds herself asking a LOT of questions after she agrees to transport a seller's loved one named Bruce.
Todd and Tamera take on some Monsters in a move that proves to be anything but cinematic.
A giant dog toy has Todd and Tamera chasing their tails as they try to navigate trailer issues and engine trouble.
Marc takes on an antique camper and Dusty transports a sculpture.
A giant, but simple chair provides some oversized complications for Jarrett when it won't fit down the stairs.
Jessica Samko wins a bizarre carnival type attraction, but things go fowl, when she lands a side load of baby swans.
Samko reluctantly teams up with Jenn after Jenn bids way above her weight class.
Dusty's sensitive side is called on when he nets the job of transporting hundreds of live butterflies.
Marc is at the helm of relaunching a massive homemade houseboat but the family's history with the boat, and Marc's stormy attitude, threaten to sink the job before it ever reaches water
After winning a black light putt-putt golf course, Jenn's game is tested when she realizes that for her run, "MINI-golf" is a misnomer.
Mike attends the PBR in Chicago, Illinois, to train and work as a bull fighter.
Mike attends the SkillsUSA National Competition in Kansas City, Missouri, and tries his hand at welding, cake decorating, and broadcasting. Spoiler Alert: He’s not good!
Mike visits the Two-Bit Circus in Los Angeles, California, where disruptive innovators have added an A to STEM to make it STEAM—Science, Technology, Engineering, Art, and Math.
Mike meets the man who is pulling millions of pounds of trash from America’s waterways.
In this two-episode segment, Mike and his crew take you deep inside the workings of the largest ship in the US Navy, the USS John Stennis.
From the mess hall to the flight deck, Mike does every job on the ship, and along the way learns the history of these floating cities.
Mike learns the history of lowrider culture from the Fuentes brothers of Homies Hydraulics and gets tricked into competing in a crazy car-jumping contest.
Mike learns the ups and downs of bobblehead making from the folks at Royal Bobble in Atlanta.
Mike does some serious bird watching at the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences and assists Lead Ornithologist John Gerwin in teaching the next generation of bird lovers.
Mike embraces his inner K9 and learns firsthand how dogs get trained by master trainer and owner of Action K9 Sports, Terry Parrish.
Mike visits the Dragon Forge shop where father and son blacksmiths Craig and Rory May teach him how to bend steel using old-time, anvil-banging, heavy metal forging.
In the perfect metaphor for life, ice sculptors Jeanne and Max Zuleta specialize in carving works of art out of a constantly decaying material—ice.
Mike and Linda Watson, known as the Prairie Dog Lady, find and capture prairie dogs from areas where they are pests and relocate them to areas where they will thrive and create a healthy prairie.
Mike visits Wolf Stunt Ranch, where he learns everything there is to know about pyrotechnics, explosives, and gun safety to be used in films and TV, and then he blows things up real good!
Mike joins the Chicago Fire Department, Engine 13 and learns firsthand how they perform ice rescues while swimming in icy waters.
In his hometown of Baltimore, Mike visits the Edgar Allen Poe house and meets Poe impersonator David Keltz, who has committed over 50,000 of Poe’s words to memory.

Joe hires an outsider to whip Buffalo into shape – starting with Mikey. Gord and Sean’s DC-3 delivery to the High Arctic goes awry when blizzard conditions and a broken oil cooler force an emergency landing.

Buffalo gets into the stunt flying business, re-enacting a famous WWII bombing raid with a DC-4. A hole in the C-46’s exhaust system forces Devan to decide whether or not to shut down an engine mid-flight.

Frustrated with the constant drama at Buffalo, Chuck quits. Joe clashes with the maintenance department when a series of delays puts the important sale of a Canso aircraft in jeopardy. Mikey goes on an ATV hunting trip.
